home_intro: Scan the QR codes hidden around the building. Every code comes with a question about IT. Answer it to fill your spot in the bar at the top.
game_step_unknown_code: We don't recognise this QR code. Please try again.
game_step_2_hint: Where does it smell like coffee?
game_step_4_hint: Where people build, code and tinker.
game_step_5_hint: High up in the building, with a view.
game_step_1_answer_b: A part of your laptop, like its memory
game_step_1_answer_c: A step-by-step plan to solve a problem
game_step_1_answer_d: A programming language made by Google
game_step_1_explanation: An algorithm is a series of clear steps, just like a recipe. Computers follow algorithms for almost everything: from your search results to the route in your navigation app.
game_step_2_question: How many different values can a single bit have?
game_step_2_explanation: A bit is 0 or 1: on or off. With 8 bits (one byte) you can already make 256 combinations. Everything on your computer, from photos to music, is ultimately stored as bits.
game_step_3_question: What do you use HTML for?
game_step_3_answer_a: To build the structure and content of a web page
game_step_3_explanation: HTML describes what is on a web page: headings, text, images and links. CSS gives the page its design, and JavaScript makes it interactive.
game_step_4_question: You get an email from 'your bank' with a link to log in quickly. What is this most likely?
game_step_4_answer_d: Phishing: an attempt to steal your data
game_step_4_explanation: In phishing, criminals pretend to be a trusted party to get your password or bank details. Don't click the link; go to your bank's website or app yourself. Cybersecurity is an important field within IT.
game_step_5_question: What do we mean by 'the cloud'?
game_step_5_answer_b: Storage and software on servers you use over the internet
game_step_5_answer_c: A program that forecasts the weather
game_step_5_answer_d: A memory card in your laptop
game_step_5_explanation: The cloud is made up of large data centres full of servers. Do you store photos online or work together in a shared document? Then you're using the cloud.
game_step_6_question: How does an AI model, like a chatbot, learn?
game_step_6_answer_a: It comes up with everything by itself
game_step_6_answer_b: A programmer types in all the answers beforehand
game_step_6_answer_c: It recognises patterns in lots of example data
game_step_6_answer_d: It reads your thoughts in real time
game_step_6_explanation: An AI model is trained on huge amounts of examples and learns patterns from them. That's why good data matters so much: from bad examples, a model learns bad things too.
game_intro_title: Welcome to the HU Open Day scavenger hunt!
game_intro_body: QR codes are placed around the building. Scan them with your phone's camera. Every code comes with a multiple-choice question about IT: no prior knowledge needed! After answering you'll see right away whether you were right, and your spot in the progress bar fills up. Any order is fine.
